sources.citation: Bhawnani, Murli D. 1979. Descriptive analysis of Thari (a dialect of Sindhi language). PhD thesis, Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, Poona. vii+257 pp. (Shodhganga hdl 10603/169640; chapters downloaded: title, preface, contents, ch.1 Introduction pp.1-6, ch.2 Phonology pp.7-51, ch.5 Differences between Thari and standard Sindhi pp.137-160, bibliography)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing. Ch.2 phoneme inventory (p.8) lists 'Suprasegmental phonemes: Nasalization ~; Internal juncture /+/; Terminal juncture /(down-arrow)(up-arrow)/' only; sections 2.3.2.4-2.3.2.6 (pp.23-24) describe nasalization, internal open juncture ('marked by the prolongation of the vowel in the pre-junctural position') and terminal pitch contours; 2.4 allophones condition vowel length by syllable type/word shape; 2.7 'Syllabic system' (pp.49-51) gives syllable patterns up to five syllables. No word 'stress' or 'accent' occurs in ch.2 or ch.5 (text layer a full-text search for stress/accent incl. sc…
Consonant and vowel inventories only; nothing on stress. References: Ethnologue, LSI VIII.1, Omniglot, Laghari 2005 (ResearchGate), Dawn 2009, Kachru 2006.
